recipes.name: Hungarian Cucumber Salad
ingredients_raw: 2 large seedless English cucumbers, sliced thin
0.5 teaspoon ground black pepper, or to taste

steps.text: Lightly toss cucumber slices, onion slices, and chopped dill together in a large bowl.
Pour vinegar over cucumber mixture; toss to coat.
Pour oil over cucumber mixture; toss to coat.
Season with salt and black pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Hungarian Cucumber Salad
raw_recipe.description: Cucumber, onion, and dill get a quick dressing in vinegar and oil for a simple, Hungarian-inspired cucumber salad.

review.reviewBody:
This recipe is very similar to the one I learned from my mum. I used apple cider vinegar and a mix of chopped fresh and dried dill. I seasoned with salt and pepper when I added the vinegar and dill. My mum would salt the cucumber and onions first and let them sit in a sieve for about 15-30 minutes then squeeze out the excess water before transferring to a serving bowl and adding the dressing. Doing it the way it says in the recipe just cuts about a half hour of prep time, the result is the same. Yummy!
To give the salad a bit more colour I also added a bit of thinly sliced red bell pepper. 
Another option is to also add some cherry tomatoes, crumbled feta cheese and kalamata olives. The salad goes from Hungarian to Greek!

this is the cucumber sald that I remember from my childhood! To give it a bit more flavor make one or two of the teaspoons of vinegar blasamic or some other flavored vinegar (preferabley whitish). I prefer less salt as well.

This was tasty. I made a half a recipe and got about 4 servings. I used a sweet onion, but cut the amount in half. I also halved the salt and pepper and just sprinkled additional salt to taste. I took the pic. and realized I forgot to add the dill. I just added 2 pinches of dry for half the recipe. It improved the flavor. For some reason, this salad tasted like non tart pickle slices. It tastes great cold and just made, but like most salads with salt I didn't care for it after it sat. I would definitely make it right before serving.

Omitted the oil and added 1/2 cup sour cream also used white balsamic vinegar. I did this because my friend loves the sour cream version but there was none with fresh dill which I had already purchased. It came out great! Everyone loved it.

Delicious. Followed the recipe with the exception, I used white wine vinegar. The Fresh dill is the main actor. Don’t skimp on the dill. The cucumbers get better and better everyday, so don’t be a fraid to make a day ahead. Thank You for sharing.
Add 3 tablespoons sugar, dill is optional bur delightful, and you have our generations-old recipe. Just made it for a cousin, it brought back great memories.

Love this! I've made it 5 times already. Was interested because it doesn't have sugar or sweetener like many cucumber salad recipes. I made as written the first time (used dried dill). Since then have increased vinegar to half cup . I used regular cucumbers once, was still good but the English is better. I always slice paper thin with a mandolin. Worth the effort. Right too about tossing in vinegar first. So good, and right again about letting it mellow for a couple days. The cucumber aroma just makes your mouth water and the taste is just as good. Of course I'm a cucumber fanatic. This is perfect for me. Thanks!
This was great. I substituted rice and balsamic vinegar instead of white vinegar.

Ate this salad a lot growing up in central NJ, made the same way as directed...BUT if you take out the vinegar and oil and instead use sour cream OR plain yogurt to taste it is also cool and refreshing.
Amazing!! Used Wildtree Garlic infused grapeseed oil instead of vegetable oil and it added a superior flavor to the whole dish!

This tasted light and fresh! After reading other reviews I added another tablespoon of vinegar (I used 2T of white vinegar and 2T of red wine vinegar). I was expecting more "bite" with the vinegar, but still it was pretty mild. My husband asked if I was going to put Italian dressing on this and I laughed and said "No". I guess he liked it since he went back for seconds!
I add some sugar to taste, delicious. I am half Hungarian and half Ukrainian
Easy to make, very nice. I added a small bit of sugar because it was a bit sharp for me., but very nice.

Let it sit over night, as I normally do wen I make cucumber salad. It tasted mostly bitter and had an overpowering dill taste. I ended up squeezing as much of the liquid out as possible and added red wine vinegar and olive oil to make it edible. Luckily I checked in the morning, and our guests didn't arrive until evening.
I make this often in the summer. Delicious.
We love this recipe at our house. I make it often, exactly as written. Perfection!
Made a s was .It was a change from the other way. Thank you.
I am not sure what went wrong. Maybe the cukes were bitter? It was not a favorite among the crowd.
This recipe received a full approval from my Hungarian friend who said the taste is exactly the way he remembers. Thank you for the recipe.
Nice fresh side dish. Simple and quick. I loved it.
